requirement: Implement SafeResponseConsumer that guarantees explicit connection release via await response.release() on non-200 status codes, decoding errors, or early stream termination, preventing connection pool starvation and socket leaks in high-throughput aiohttp applications.
skeleton: SafeResponseConsumer class with fetch_payload and read_header_value methods enforcing response release.
caption: An aiohttp response consumer that always returns the underlying connection to the pool, whatever path the read takes. BadStatusError subclasses Exception. ResponseStreamConsumer.fetch_json_safe(session, url) awaits session.get to obtain the response and, inside a try block, awaits response.release() and raises BadStatusError naming the status when the status is not 200; otherwise it returns the awaited JSON. Any exception raised in that block, including a decoding failure from response.json, awaits release before being re-raised unchanged, so a malformed body cannot leave the connection checked out. Release is awaited rather than merely called, since calling it without await only creates a coroutine that never runs, and release is used rather than close so the connection goes back to the pool instead of being destroyed. read_header_value(session, url, header_key) fetches the response, returns the named header or None, and awaits release in a finally block without ever reading the body, so a header-only probe does not strand its socket. The fixture uses mocked responses and asserts that a 500 raises BadStatusError with at least one awaited release, that a ValueError reporting Invalid JSON from the decoder propagates after release was awaited, that reading the header returns secret-123 with exactly one awaited release, and that a successful fetch returns ok True without ever calling close.

rationale.teaches: Guaranteed response release: await release on non-200, on decode errors, on any exception, and after reading a header, so pooled connections return to the pool.
rationale.why: An unreleased response keeps its connection checked out; with a small pool the next request blocks. The fixture counts release calls per path with a fake response.

candidates.why_wrong: release is never called, so every response keeps its connection checked out until garbage collection.
release is called without await, so the coroutine is created and discarded and the connection stays held.
read_header_value returns the header without releasing, so a header-only read leaks a connection.
Only BadStatusError triggers release, so a decoding error leaks the connection.
close is used instead of release, so the connection is destroyed instead of returned to the pool.
